text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Canary deployment rlv2-ratecap v2.3.1 showing spike in 429s across prod-us-east-1 and prod-eu-west-1. 5xx rate stable. Paging oncall.

alex: saw the page. looking at dashboards now. can someone post the canary flags/rollout id?

maria: rollout id 2026-03-15-rlv2-canary-7. stats show 20% of traffic to canary, 30s p50 latency unchanged but 429s up ~12% overall in those regions.

sam: @alex i'm on-call for infra today. handing off — i'm taking lead. sam here.

alex: thx sam. assigning to you. quick question: is this the new exemptions logic that landed in the ratecap service?

jess: yes. PR #4823 introduced exemption propagation to the new RLv2 path. suspect: exemptions not being read for routed canary nodes -> over-throttle.

kevin: logs show token_accounting counter mismatch on canary instances. snippet from mate-rl-canary-3: 
```
WARN ratecap: token_accounting: expected exemptions=124 actual=0 tenant=acme-inc request_id=xyz123
```

alex: oof. that would cause customers with exemptions to get 429s. any customer-reported tickets?

support-bot: New support alerts: 8 customers reporting 429 errors in the last 10m. Top affected: acme-inc, payroll-corp, retailio. Priority: P1 for acme-inc (realtime search failing).

sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip canary kill-switch to direct traffic off canary, 2) rollback rlv2 change at infra level, 3) add temporary bypass to exemption check (riskier). recommend 1 then 2.

jess: agreed. kill-switch is lowest-risk and instantaneous. admin flag name is `rlv2_canary_route_enabled`.

alex: how to flip? i can run if you confirm command.

kevin: admin API call (internal):
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/flags/rlv2_canary_route_enabled" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"value":false}'
```

sam: do it alex. i'm watching traffic and will validate exemptions count.

alex: running now.

alex: `> POST /flags/rlv2_canary_route_enabled 200 OK` :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: :information_source: Kill-switch flipped for rlv2 canary routing by alex. Canary traffic should drain to stable pool over next 30s.

kevin: beginning validation: checking token_accounting metrics on stable nodes now.

jess: canary instances will still be alive but get 0 new traffic. we should schedule a rollback of the change to prevent re-enabled rollout.

sam: customer 429s dropping. support-bot, can you recheck active tickets?

support-bot: Follow-up: 429 reports dropped to 1 for acme-inc (retry window). Notifying impacted customers that mitigation is in progress.

alex: nice. sam, can you confirm exemptions counts on stable vs canary pre/post?

kevin: confirmed: stable nodes show exemptions count matching expected (acme-inc=124, payroll-corp=87). Canary nodes had zero before; after kill-switch they stopped receiving traffic and counters are stable but still zero. So bug is in exemptions propagation on canary path.

maria: next step: rollback the PR in the canary gating pipeline and create a patch that ensures exemptions header gets forwarded to rlv2 path. jess, can you own the fix?

jess: I will. starting a branch now. probable root cause: header name mismatch `X-Exemptions` vs `x-exemptions` casing in new code path. will write unit + integration tests.

sam: ops note: i'm keeping the canary instances up but drained. will also pin autoscaler to avoid churn until rollback complete.

alex: customer comms: i'll coordinate with support and send a short incident ack to affected customers: explanation + ETA for fix (ETA 2 hours for rollback + validation).

support-bot: Draft message for customers approved by ops: "We detected a canary routing regression that temporarily prevented exemption rules from applying for a subset of traffic. We've disabled the canary and are rolling back the change. Service is recovering; we'll follow up when fully resolved."

kevin: monitoring shows global 429 rate back to baseline within 90s of kill-switch. good.

jess: PR #4850 opened to revert changes in routing layer. linking for reviewers.

maria: once PR is merged we'll redeploy canary with tests. until then, leave kill-switch off.

sam: handing back to alex for postmortem/wrap. alex, you're on postmortem owner for initial draft. will add jess for root cause and kevin for metrics.

alex: accepted. timeline/notes:
- 1882345678: incident-bot alert triggered by ratecap 429 spike
- 1882345685: oncall sam accepted
- 1882345692: kill-switch flipped (rlv2_canary_route_enabled=false)
- 1882345703: 429 rates returned to baseline
- 1882345750: PR #4850 opened to rollback

alex: follow-ups:
- jess: patch + integration tests for exemption header propagation (owner jess)
- kevin: metric dashboards to split exemptions by routing-path (owner kevin)
- support: customer follow-ups and post-incident email (owner support)
- ops/sam: create playbook entry for immediate canary kill-switch steps (owner sam)

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident acknowledged as mitigated. Please update the thread with timeline and links to PRs/alerts for postmortem.

jess: I'll add repro and unit tests. expected PR merge in ~45m.

sam: leaving monitoring watchers. passing back to alex.

alex: thanks team. will draft incident postmortem and ping channel when ready. closing thread for live ops; reopen if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
